summary.text: Jodie Minor is an independent candidate for Alabama State Senate District 21 in the November 3, 2026 general election, running against incumbent Republican Gerald Allen.
A retired U.S. Army officer and preacher, he says his priorities include rural health care access, education, law enforcement and economic opportunity.

paragraphs.text: Jodie Minor was born in Carrollton, Alabama, and served in the U.S. Army from 2004 to 2024.

He earned a high school diploma from Carrollton High School, a bachelor's degree from Athens State University, an M.B.A. from Alabama A&M University, a master's degree in legislative affairs from George Washington University and a Master of Divinity from Virginia Union University.

His career experience includes working as a military officer and preacher, and he has served as a congressional fellow for Representative Robert Aderholt and as a human capital director for the White House's National Security Council.
In a Ballotpedia survey, he said he served two combat tours in Baghdad, leads congregational ministry at the Pickens County Jail and is a member of Pine Grove Baptist Church.
Ballotpedia lists Minor among withdrawn or disqualified candidates in the Democratic primary; he is on the general election ballot as an independent.
In the survey, he said he wants to address the rural health care crisis, including hospital closures in District 21, and to represent veterans in Montgomery.

He also said Alabama's schools and learning programs should be linked to job-market demands, and that gun laws should honor Second Amendment rights while putting law enforcement and community safety first.
